To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed recursive binary neural network learning algorithm can reduce the data storage requirement for the weights by 8× to 16× for deep and convolutional network models, achieving better classification performance.
we present a storage-efficient learning framework for training binary neural networks with a limited amount of data storage.
the proposed model can train a larger network with the same amount of on-chips storage and/or achieve the similar accuracy with less data storage than the conventional binary learning model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficient use of limited on-chip storage for neural network classifiers on embedded and mobile devices.
the development of a storage-efficient training model for neural networks.
the efficient storage of weights in binary neural networks, which is a key to enable the deployment of deep neural network learning on resource-constrained mobile and embedded devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model achieves a better classification accuracy with less on-chip data-storage requirement than the existing binary neural network learning algorithms.

the proposed recursive binary neural network learning method achieves 2-bit/ weight data storage requirement, 4× storage savings to obtain the same classification accuracy, or 6× data storage savings to achieve similar classification accuracy.
the proposed model achieves better accuracy and energy-efficiency with a given storage limit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed model enables a device with 2-bit data storage for weights to train and use a larger number of parameters than the conventional learning model, achieving better classification performance.
the proposed model enables training a neural network classifier having a larger number of parameters with a limited on-chip data-storage constraint.
we have developed an energy-efficient learning model for embedded and mobile applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model can train a neural network classifier having a large number of weights with a limited on-chip storage.
the proposed model can train a neural network classifier having more weights on a chip with the same or less on-chip data memory than the conventional learning model.
the data storage of weights in the training phase can be recycled, and the data storage requirement of weights can be significantly reduced by using a recursive binary neural network model.
